title: Ranking architecture for sub-200ms personalized search
prompt: You're ranking results from a huge document index. Each query must return personalized, relevant results. How do you architect the ranking pipeline?
constraint: Sub-200ms end-to-end latency while delivering personalization and relevance over a huge index.

options.why: A cheap recall stage (inverted index / ANN) trims the huge index to a few hundred candidates in milliseconds, then the expensive personalized ML model scores only the top-K. The model never touches the full index, so you get full personalization and relevance while staying inside the sub-200ms budget — the standard web-scale answer and the best fit.

Personalization and relevance would be excellent, but running a learning-to-rank model across a huge index on every query is orders of magnitude over the latency budget. No amount of hardware makes per-query full-index ML scoring fit sub-200ms — it violates the constraint.

Serving is trivially fast, but a global precomputed order can't personalize per user or per query and goes stale between rebuilds. It sacrifices the personalization and relevance the constraint explicitly demands, so speed alone doesn't save it.

Latency stays bounded and you get some personalization on top of a precomputed base, so it's defensible. But a shallow re-scoring layer over a static base can't match the relevance of a full ML re-rank on freshly retrieved candidates — weaker than two-stage retrieval on the relevance half of the constraint.
